Potentially another miscarriage

I’ve had two losses this year, a missed miscarriage at 9 weeks in April and a chemical pregnancy in July. After the July loss my OBGYN ordered some tests for me (karyotype, clotting, thyroid, carrier screening etc) and my husband went to a urologist who specializes in male infertility. Everything came back fine for me but my husband was diagnosed with bilateral varicocele which kind of seemed like good news because at least it meant we knew why things were going wrong rather than just “bad luck”. But he got his sperm analysis results recently and everything (count, motility) looked good, and we thought that the DNA fragmentation must be the issue. Then his DNA fragmentation results came back, and everything is basically fine. He’s under the threshold for DFI and borderline for oxidative stress and normal for high DNA stainability. This all sounds good except now we’re back at the start of wondering why we keep having losses. He has been taking more antioxidant supplements over the last few months which may have improved his results since he just did the sperm analysis recently.

Anyways while we were waiting on all this I got a positive pregnancy test and we were so excited, we were just trying to be hopeful that we got a healthy sperm this time. I had an ultrasound last week at 7w1d and baby was measuring on target and had a heart rate of 125 bpm. I had another appointment this week at 8w2d because of the previous missed miscarriage so my OBGYN wanted to keep a close eye on progression. Our baby again was measuring on target but the heart rate had decreased to 85 bpm… my doctor said it should be around 110 or higher by now. She said it’s still possible that this is a temporary blip and the heart rate could go up again but she also told me not to get my hopes up and this is not normal. I have a follow up ultrasound next week but now I have a feeling that I’ll have another miscarriage this time, which would be my third loss overall 😕 Now we’re not even sure if it’s related to sperm quality or just a random issue again. Our first miscarriage in April was due to a chromosomal abnormality (Turner syndrome). 

I’m really dreading the idea of having another loss, it feels like I’ve been pregnant or recovering from a miscarriage for so long now. 

I’m curious if anyone has been through something similar? Also curious about anyone who dealt with the varicocele situation, my husband has been taking CoQ10 since February and recently started NAC and L-carnitine in June, so I think these may have improved his results but not 100% sure.

My wife made the difficult decision to have an induction abortion. The procedure itself went as expected, and she is physically fine. Emotionally, we are both still grieving. So much blood

I had a miscarriage at 12 + 3 weeks before and that was carried out in the hospital and the cramps were horrendous. This time I'm 7 + 5 weeks and it was a blighted ovum so I thought this would be easier and there wouldn't be so much blood. Online everyone seemed to just speak of it as a heavy period and seeing as my periods are heavy anyway I thought I'd be fine. 
Oh my god. 
First off, the cramping started yesterday when I was halfway up a mountain which didn't help. There was a lot of blood, with a few decent clots in it. The cramping made me almost throw up so I figured that was it. Overnight there wasn't much blood, then today it was more like a "normal" period so I thought "this must be the tail end." 
Then I went out to an evening even thing and bled through a towel suddenly - and I mean suddenly. One moment it had a spot or two, the next it was like it had been dyed red. There wasn't a white patch on it. 
"Oh, that must be it!" I thought. Changed, washed my hands, then jumped immediately back on the toilet again and felt actual lumps passing. The pain is low now. Cramping, but really nothing worth mentioning. 
"Phew, good job I was in a bathroom" I thought, and texted my husband to let him know he might need to pick me up early. Less than 3mins later I texted him again in all caps because I felt the next handful of lumps drop out. He picked me up - it's less than 3mins by car and I'd walked in - and by the time we got home I'd soaked through my jeans. I needed to sit on a plastic bag in the car. 
It's still all just flowing out in bursts. I'm sat on the toilet with medium low cramps bit the surprising thing is the stinging. It feels like an open wound that hurts when the air or my urine gets on it. 
Maybe I shouldn't have been so naive as I have miscarried before, but no one warned me, and honestly I just figured as nothing ever grew, passing a tiny egg sac wouldn't be such a big deal! 
Anyway, if anyone else googled "miscarriage stinging" like I did and found this, you are not the only one. And I'm sorry you're going through it and I just hope you habe someone with you.

My story: laminaria and D&E at 16 weeks

Wanted to write my experience out since I’ve found it helpful to read others. I had a missed miscarriage, diagnosed at 15 weeks. My boy stopped growing somewhere between 13-14 weeks, and I had a D&E a week later.

Yesterday (day before the D&E) I had two large laminaria sticks placed to help dilate my cervix. I asked for lidocaine because I read that it can be really painful, but to be honest the lidocaine shots hurt anyway. I’m not great with needles, and still not sure which kind of pain would have been better. I had cramping the rest of the day. Tried Advil, heat pad, and low dose edibles but was still pretty bad so asked for something stronger and my OB prescribed me naproxen (basically strong Aleve), which worked a little better and helped me sleep. By this morning the cramping was better. I was worried the laminaria would trigger labor or contractions but my OB said this doesn’t happen often in her experience and it didn’t with me- just some spotting the next morning. 

Today I got to the hospital and (sorry tmi) pooped and the gauze and laminaria sticks slid out into the toilet. I got checked in, and then the worst part of the experience happened- getting the damn IV put in! It took so long and the nurse kept talking about the process and I think that triggered my vasovagal response and after the IV started I could tell I was going to pass out (happens a lot). So I passed out, the anesthesiologist happened to be there and was insisting I had a petite mal seizure during it (my eyes rolled back and I was convulsing) and thought I should get a neurology consult. But in the end, with my history of passing out many times in my life and the fact that they already started the process with the laminaria, my OB thankfully decided to go ahead with the D&E that morning, seizure be damned. (Later I read that people who pass out have convulsions pretty frequently, so that made me feel better. I also got a work up for this decades ago and they couldn’t find anything.) 

Anyway - they put me under general for the D&E. I woke up and waited in bed a while until I was less groggy. The nurse had me pee and then I was discharged pretty soon with my husband. 

I feel so much better now. I had a long nap at home and haven’t felt this good physically since the early days of the pregnancy. No more nausea, no cramping, barely any bleeding yet. Feel like I can continue the emotional processing part of this without all the anticipation of the procedure, the feeling that my dead baby is inside me, or the pregnancy fatigue and nausea. I’ve had a D&C before and had some bleeding for weeks after, so thinking that might start in the next couple days. 

It’s pretty weird to just feel “normal” again physically, actually. Makes me feel a little disconnected from my baby. Ordered an embroidery project (the flowers of his due date month), so looking forward to working on that.

natural mc after mmc and what i wish i knew before

I wanted to write up my miscarriage experience for those who don’t know what to expect. My care team did not give me a heads up at all, so everything I learned (I mean everything, from diagnosis to delivery, was from Reddit and experience).

10/1: Found out sac measured 2 weeks behind, no fetus in the sac. My OB sent me to high risk after noticing my HCG drop, but did not diagnose as mmc.

10/7: Follow up scan with MFM, they did not do the first ultrasound so they wanted to monitor for another week despite levels going down.

10/13: MFM sees “something” in sac (blood clots) but can’t figure out what, so they wanted to monitor for another week. Meanwhile, I still have pregnancy symptoms as this was a MMC/blighted ovum.

10/13: That day I start spotting brown and red, it picks up through the day but I’m hardly spotting on underwear. 

10/15: After spotting for a few days, the bleeding picks up around 830pm. The cramps ramp up and I start bleeding heavily. Around 930 I had passed multiple clots around the same size or smaller than a golf ball. I would probably have filled a pad but I sat on the toilet the whole time to avoid clotting in my underwear. I believe the key is you don’t want to be filling two pads per hour for over two hours (edited) double check that but I felt physically fine (not lightheaded or faint) so I was confident I was okay. 

At 1030 ish I’m still cramping and passing clots. I passed probably 7-8 large clots and lots of smaller ones (maybe 10 or more), and lots of continuous blood. I was drinking tons of electrolytes and took my prenatals for the iron. I also took a shower to get some heat on my back. Also had a bowl of cereal to keep my energy up! Please eat if you can. 

At 1130 I start CONTRACTING. Why did nobody tell me I’d contract?! It felt exactly like the beginning of labor with my first. One minute contractions, 30 seconds apart. I was in agony, so I took a Tylenol extra strength (I’m not sure it did anything, if you have anything stronger, I’d take it lol). I labored on the toilet but was starting to feel sore and swollen from 3-4 hours on the toilet, so I put my pants on and labored on all fours with my husband massaging my back. I had to try to push the sac out. You will have to try to labor down.

Around 12 I went to the toilet and felt a HUGE drop, I screamed and the sac came out. About the size of 2 golf balls and like people here have said, it is grayish/white in color. Surgical abortion - my experience

I (23F) am from the UK and I had an abortion back in January of this year. I thought I'd share my experience for anyone who is nervous to get one done or wondering what it feels like.

Some context: in the back end of 2024 and early 2025, I was going through a really rough time. I'd been in and out of hospital for mental health reasons, my 4 year relationship ended up being a total lie, and I'd just moved into my new home by myself.

With all of that going on, I literally had no idea I was pregnant until I took a pregnancy test prior to getting my IUD removed... yeah, you can imagine the shock. IUDs gradually lose effectiveness as the years go on and mine was at the very end of its life cycle, so I shouldn't really have been surprised.

In hindsight, there were some symptoms that I ignored. I'd been getting bad heartburn and felt super nauseous all the time, but my appetite had been on and off those past few weeks. I thought it was just my body readjusting to getting regular food again. I'd gained some weight BUT, again, my eating habits had been all over the place and I hadn't been exercising as much as I should have, so I just assumed that was the cause. More fool me lmao. Don't do what I did and brush off symptoms like that - it's rarely ever "nothing".

When the test came back positive, I went straight to my GP to confirm and was estimated to be around 15 weeks. We had a discussion of my options but I was pretty set that I wanted to terminate. I'd had zero intention of falling pregnant in the first place and knew I was not in the right frame of mind to undergo pregnancy/labour or raise a child. I'm a type-one diabetic as well and pregnancies require *immaculate* control of blood sugars to ensure everything goes smoothly. I'd love to be a mum one day but this was not my time. I was alone and unprepared and I was not physically or mentally fit enough to go through with it.

My abortion was pencilled in ten days after my discussion with the GP. I opted for a surgical termination. You *can* technically terminate using medications up to the full legal limit, but I opted for a surgical abortion just to be safe as they don't usually recommend medical abortions over 10 weeks. My sister had gotten a surgical abortion over a decade ago so I knew roughly what to expect, but my GP had a lengthy chat with me in advance and how I should prepare on the day. She was an absolute gem and spoke with absolutely no judgement or condescension. 

Might be controversial but I never told either potential dad. According to the dates, there was some crossover, meaning the father could've either been my ex (not a nice guy, to put it mildly) or a friend I'd slept with no more than twice (me and my ex had already split up, for context. Although I probably had every right to, I didn't cheat on him). I never told my friends or family either and went to my appointment alone. To this day, no one in my personal life knows about my abortion ex
